newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel negotiator enters to start talks.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel negotiator enters to start talks.

text.p: A Peruvian rebel spokesman entered a safe house opposite the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima to start a third round of talks with government negotiator Domingo Palermo, witnesses said.

A Red Cross car transported the rebel from the diplomatic residence, where the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) is holding 72 hostages for the 60th day, to the house where Palermo and talks' mediators were waiting.
The rebel was believed to be MRTA No. 2 Rolly Rojas, who has represented the group in two previous rounds of talks this week with Palermo.
Minutes earlier, Palermo and mediators had arrived at the site of the residence before assembling and entering the safe house together.

The MRTA is seeking to obtain the freedom of some 400 jailed comrades, followed by safe passage to the jungle for the hostage-takers inside the residence. But the government has flatly ruled out this demand.
It is unknown what points have been discussed in the meetings other than an agreement to continue talking.
